```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Jones 2019 related the serum exposure of olaratumab, an anti-PDGFR-alpha IgG1
antibody, to overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) in the
randomised phase 2 trial JGDG (NCT01185964) of olaratumab plus doxorubicin
versus doxorubicin alone in soft tissue sarcoma. Each endpoint was fitted twice,
once with each of two exposure metrics, giving four separately estimated
parametric time-to-event models, packaged as four files:

* `modellib("Jones_2019_olaratumab_os_cmin1")` -- OS driven by the trough
  concentration at the end of cycle 1 (Cmin1, Table 2).
* `modellib("Jones_2019_olaratumab_os_cavg")` -- OS driven by the average
  concentration over the patient's entire treatment (Cavg, Table 2).
* `modellib("Jones_2019_olaratumab_pfs_cmin1")` -- PFS driven by Cmin1
  (Table 3).
* `modellib("Jones_2019_olaratumab_pfs_cavg")` -- PFS driven by Cavg (Table 3).

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Jones_2019_olaratumab_os_cmin1"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00280-018-3723-4>

All four models have a constant (exponential) baseline hazard, reduced by an
inhibitory sigmoid Imax function of the olaratumab exposure $C$:

$$h = h_0 \, (1 + \theta_{ECOG} \, ECOG_{\ge 1}) \, (1 + \theta_{1L} \, LINE_{1L})
\left(1 - \frac{I_{max} \, C^{\gamma}}{EC_{50}^{\gamma} + C^{\gamma}}\right),
\qquad S(t) = e^{-h t}.$$

The ECOG and prior-line factors are present only in the OS models; no covariate
was retained for PFS. The Hill coefficient $\gamma$ was fixed to 8 in all four
models. Time is in days and the exposure in ug/mL; the doxorubicin-alone arm
has $C = 0$ and therefore the baseline hazard alone. The exposures are
individual predictions from the population PK model of Mo 2018, packaged as
`modellib("Mo_2018_olaratumab")`, so the survival models carry no PK layer of
their own: `CTROUGH` (Cmin1) or `CAV` (Cavg) is supplied as a data column.

# Population

Survival data came from all 133 randomised patients with histologically
confirmed locally advanced or metastatic soft tissue sarcoma: 66 received
olaratumab 15 mg/kg IV on days 1 and 8 plus doxorubicin 75 mg/m2 on day 1 of
each 21-day cycle, and 67 received doxorubicin alone, for up to eight cycles.
Olaratumab could continue alone after the doxorubicin cycles until progression.
Tumour response was assessed every 6 weeks by RECIST 1.1. Individual olaratumab
exposures were available for 62 patients of the experimental arm (Table 4).
Jones 2019 does not tabulate baseline demographics; the trial's observed
medians, quoted in its Introduction, were OS 26.5 versus 14.7 months
(HR 0.46) and PFS 6.6 versus 4.1 months (HR 0.67).

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Jones_2019_olaratumab_os_cmin1"))$population)
```

# Hazard ratio against exposure

The hazard ratio for olaratumab against no olaratumab is `hr_drug`. This
replicates the red curves of Figures 1b and 2b.

```{r hr-curves}
models <- c(
  "Jones_2019_olaratumab_os_cmin1", "Jones_2019_olaratumab_os_cavg",
  "Jones_2019_olaratumab_pfs_cmin1", "Jones_2019_olaratumab_pfs_cavg"
)
exposure_col <- c(
  Jones_2019_olaratumab_os_cmin1 = "CTROUGH",
  Jones_2019_olaratumab_os_cavg = "CAV",
  Jones_2019_olaratumab_pfs_cmin1 = "CTROUGH",
  Jones_2019_olaratumab_pfs_cavg = "CAV"
)
mods <- lapply(models, function(m) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(m)))
names(mods) <- models

# Evaluate hr_drug on a concentration grid: one subject per concentration,
# a single observation at day 1.
hr_grid <- function(m, conc) {
  d <- data.frame(id = seq_along(conc), time = 1, evid = 0, cmt = "cumhaz")
  d[[exposure_col[[m]]]] <- conc
  d$ECOG_GE1 <- 0
  d$LINE_1L <- 0
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mods[[m]], events = d, returnType = "data.frame")
  data.frame(model = m, conc = conc, hr_drug = s$hr_drug)
}
conc <- seq(0, 350, by = 1)
hr_df <- bind_rows(lapply(models, hr_grid, conc = conc)) |>
  mutate(
    endpoint = ifelse(grepl("_os_", model), "OS", "PFS"),
    metric = ifelse(grepl("cmin1", model), "Cmin1", "Cavg")
  ) |>
  filter(!(metric == "Cmin1" & conc > 200))

ggplot(hr_df, aes(conc, hr_drug, colour = endpoint)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_x") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Olaratumab exposure (ug/mL)", y = "Predicted hazard ratio",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the hazard-ratio curves of Figures 1b and 2b of Jones 2019."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

Three properties of these curves can be read from the paper. The plateau is
`1 - Imax`: the Results describe a maximal improvement in the OS hazard ratio
of about 75% and an Imax of about 0.60 for PFS. The hazard ratio is 1 at zero
exposure. And the EC50 values were reported to coincide with the 25th
percentile of the exposure distribution for OS and with its median for PFS;
the quartile boundaries are printed in Table 4.

```{r hr-checks}
hr_at <- function(m, c) hr_grid(m, c)$hr_drug
ini_of <- function(m) {
  x <- mods[[m]]$theta
  c(imax = exp(x[["limax"]]), ec50 = exp(x[["lec50"]]))
}
hr_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(models, function(m) {
  p <- ini_of(m)
  data.frame(
    model = m,
    hr_zero = hr_at(m, 0),
    hr_ec50 = hr_at(m, p[["ec50"]]),
    expected_hr_ec50 = 1 - p[["imax"]] / 2,
    hr_plateau = hr_at(m, 5 * p[["ec50"]]),
    expected_plateau = 1 - p[["imax"]]
  )
}))
knitr::kable(hr_tab, digits = 3)

# Table 4 quartile boundaries (ug/mL): Q1/Q2, median, Q3/Q4.
q_cmin1 <- c(q25 = 62.8, q50 = 86.9, q75 = 105.6)
q_cavg <- c(q25 = 134.4, q50 = 175.2, q75 = 249.9)
ec50_vs_quartile <- data.frame(
  model = models,
  ec50 = sapply(models, function(m) ini_of(m)[["ec50"]]),
  paper_quantile = c(q_cmin1[["q25"]], q_cavg[["q25"]], q_cmin1[["q50"]], q_cavg[["q50"]]),
  quantile_named = c("25th", "25th", "median", "median")
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (ec50 / paper_quantile - 1))
knitr::kable(ec50_vs_quartile, digits = 1, row.names = FALSE)

stopifnot(
  # hr_drug is an algebraic function of the same parameters, so these hold to
  # rounding, not to sampling noise.
  all(abs(hr_tab$hr_zero - 1) < 1e-9),
  all(abs(hr_tab$hr_ec50 - hr_tab$expected_hr_ec50) < 1e-9),
  all(abs(hr_tab$hr_plateau - hr_tab$expected_plateau) < 0.001),
  # Results: OS maximal HR improvement ~75%, PFS Imax ~0.60.
  all(abs(hr_tab$expected_plateau[1:2] - 0.25) < 0.02),
  all(abs(hr_tab$expected_plateau[3:4] - 0.40) < 0.04),
  # Results: EC50 at the 25th percentile (OS) and median (PFS) of exposure.
  all(abs(ec50_vs_quartile$pct_diff) < 6)
)
```

# Survival curves

## Analytic check of the integrated hazard

The models integrate the hazard as an ODE. With a constant hazard the survival
function must equal $e^{-h t}$ exactly, so this is a check of the ODE encoding
against its own closed form, using the same parameter values on both sides.

```{r closed-form}
grid_t <- seq(0, 1500, by = 10)
one_subject <- function(m, conc, ecog = 0, line1l = 0) {
  d <- data.frame(id = 1, time = grid_t, evid = 0, cmt = "cumhaz")
  d[[exposure_col[[m]]]] <- conc
  d$ECOG_GE1 <- ecog
  d$LINE_1L <- line1l
  d
}
cf_err <- sapply(models, function(m) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    mods[[m]],
    events = one_subject(m, conc = 100, ecog = 1, line1l = 1),
    rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, returnType = "data.frame"
  )
  max(abs(s$sur / exp(-s$hazard * s$time) - 1))
})
cf_err
stopifnot(all(cf_err < 1e-6))
```

## Virtual cohort

Jones 2019 does not publish individual exposures, but Table 4 prints the
quartile boundaries of Cmin1 and Cavg in the 62 patients with PK. The
experimental arm below draws 200 patients, 50 per quartile, uniformly within
each quartile's printed range; the doxorubicin-alone arm has zero exposure. The
paper does not report the proportions of ECOG >= 1 or of first-line patients,
so OS is shown separately for each of the four covariate combinations rather
than as an arm-level mixture.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20190101)
n_per_q <- 50
draw_quartiles <- function(b) {
  unlist(lapply(1:4, function(k) runif(n_per_q, b[k], b[k + 1])))
}
cmin1_bounds <- c(12.3, 62.8, 86.9, 105.6, 188.1) # Table 4, Cmin1 range
cavg_bounds <- c(56.0, 134.4, 175.2, 249.9, 347.3) # Table 4, Cavg range
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(4 * n_per_q),
  CTROUGH = draw_quartiles(cmin1_bounds),
  CAV = draw_quartiles(cavg_bounds)
)
summary(cohort[, c("CTROUGH", "CAV")])
```

```{r survival-sim}
grid_t <- seq(0, 1500, by = 5)
sim_arm <- function(m, arm, ecog = 0, line1l = 0, times = grid_t) {
  ids <- if (arm == "Doxorubicin") 1L else cohort$id
  d <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0, cmt = "cumhaz", ECOG_GE1 = ecog, LINE_1L = line1l)
  if (arm == "Doxorubicin") {
    d$CTROUGH <- 0
    d$CAV <- 0
  } else {
    d <- left_join(d, cohort, by = "id")
  }
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mods[[m]], events = as.data.frame(d), returnType = "data.frame")
  s |>
    group_by(time) |>
    summarise(sur = mean(sur), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(model = m, arm = arm, ECOG_GE1 = ecog, LINE_1L = line1l)
}
median_time <- function(time, sur) {
  o <- order(sur)
  approx(sur[o], time[o], xout = 0.5, ties = mean)$y
}
days_per_month <- 365.25 / 12
```

### Progression-free survival

PFS has no covariates, so the arm-level curves can be compared directly with
the trial's observed medians.

```{r pfs-curves}
pfs <- bind_rows(lapply(models[3:4], function(m) {
  bind_rows(sim_arm(m, "Doxorubicin"), sim_arm(m, "Olaratumab + doxorubicin"))
}))
ggplot(pfs, aes(time, 100 * sur, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~model) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Progression-free survival (%)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Model-predicted counterpart of Figure 2a of Jones 2019 (exposures drawn from Table 4 quartiles)."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

pfs_med <- pfs |>
  group_by(model, arm) |>
  summarise(median_days = median_time(time, sur), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    median_months = median_days / days_per_month,
    observed_months = ifelse(arm == "Doxorubicin", 4.1, 6.6),
    pct_diff = 100 * (median_months / observed_months - 1)
  )
knitr::kable(pfs_med, digits = 2)
```

The doxorubicin-alone medians are within 10% of the observed 4.1 months. The
experimental-arm medians are about 15% below the observed 6.6 months: an
exponential hazard spreads events evenly in time, while the Kaplan-Meier curve
in Figure 2a has a flat stretch between the 6-weekly tumour assessments, and
the uniform-within-quartile exposure draw is an approximation.

```{r pfs-checks}
dox <- pfs_med$arm == "Doxorubicin"
stopifnot(
  # Closed form: ln(2) / 0.00604 = 114.8 days = 3.77 months.
  all(abs(pfs_med$pct_diff[dox]) < 12),
  all(abs(pfs_med$pct_diff[!dox]) < 25),
  # Olaratumab prolongs median PFS by about half in both models.
  all(pfs_med$median_days[!dox] / pfs_med$median_days[dox] > 1.3)
)
```

### Overall survival

```{r os-curves}
strata <- expand.grid(ECOG_GE1 = 0:1, LINE_1L = 0:1)
# The longest stratum median is beyond 1500 days, so OS is solved to 3000 days
# and only the plot is clipped to the 1500 days of Figure 1a.
grid_os <- seq(0, 3000, by = 5)
os <- bind_rows(lapply(models[1:2], function(m) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(strata)), function(i) {
    bind_rows(
      sim_arm(m, "Doxorubicin", strata$ECOG_GE1[i], strata$LINE_1L[i], grid_os),
      sim_arm(m, "Olaratumab + doxorubicin", strata$ECOG_GE1[i], strata$LINE_1L[i], grid_os)
    )
  }))
})) |>
  mutate(stratum = paste0("ECOG>=1: ", ECOG_GE1, ", first line: ", LINE_1L))

ggplot(filter(os, model == "Jones_2019_olaratumab_os_cmin1"), aes(time, 100 * sur, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~stratum) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1500)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Overall survival (%)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Model-predicted counterpart of Figure 1a of Jones 2019 (Cmin1 model), by covariate stratum."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

os_med <- os |>
  group_by(model, stratum, arm) |>
  summarise(median_months = median_time(time, sur) / days_per_month, .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = median_months)
knitr::kable(os_med, digits = 1)
```

The observed doxorubicin-alone median of 14.7 months lies inside the range of
the stratum-specific predictions, and the reported effects of the covariates
are reproduced exactly: ECOG >= 1 raises the baseline hazard by 86.2% and no
prior line lowers it by 58.3% (Cmin1 model).

```{r os-checks}
os_ctrl <- os_med$Doxorubicin[os_med$model == "Jones_2019_olaratumab_os_cmin1"]
stopifnot(
  min(os_ctrl) < 14.7, max(os_ctrl) > 14.7,
  # Olaratumab lengthens the median in every stratum.
  all(os_med[["Olaratumab + doxorubicin"]] > os_med$Doxorubicin)
)

# Closed-form hazard ratios between strata: the covariate factors.
h_os <- function(ecog, line1l) {
  d <- one_subject("Jones_2019_olaratumab_os_cmin1", conc = 0, ecog = ecog, line1l = line1l)[1, ]
  rxode2::rxSolve(mods[["Jones_2019_olaratumab_os_cmin1"]], events = d, returnType = "data.frame")$hazard
}
cov_ratio <- c(ecog = h_os(1, 0) / h_os(0, 0), first_line = h_os(0, 1) / h_os(0, 0))
cov_ratio
stopifnot(
  abs(cov_ratio[["ecog"]] - 1.862) < 1e-9,
  abs(cov_ratio[["first_line"]] - 0.417) < 1e-9
)
```

# Exposure from the population PK model

The survival models take Cmin1 as an input. As a consistency check on the
exposure scale, the Mo 2018 population PK model is simulated for cycle 1 of
15 mg/kg IV over 1 hour on days 1 and 8, and the concentration at day 21 is
compared with the Cmin1 distribution of Table 4. Jones 2019 does not report the
body weight or tumour size of the sarcoma patients, so the cohort is set at the
Mo 2018 population medians (79.7 kg, 86.5 mm), with that model's
between-subject variability.

```{r mo2018-cmin1}
mo <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Mo_2018_olaratumab"))
n_pk <- 200
wt <- 79.7
dose_mg <- 15 * wt
ev_pk <- rxode2::et(
  amt = dose_mg, cmt = "central", rate = dose_mg, time = c(0, 168)
) |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 504, by = 12)) |>
  rxode2::et(id = seq_len(n_pk)) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(WT = wt, TUMSZ = 86.5)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)
pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mo, events = ev_pk, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(treatment = "olaratumab 15 mg/kg D1, D8")
```

The trough at the end of cycle 1 is computed with PKNCA as `ctrough` over the
interval 0 to 504 h.

```{r pknca}
conc_pk <- pk |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment) |>
  distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE)
dose_pk <- ev_pk |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  mutate(treatment = "olaratumab 15 mg/kg D1, D8") |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)
o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_pk, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_pk, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
o_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  o_conc, o_dose,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 504, ctrough = TRUE, cmax = TRUE)
)
o_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(o_data)
nca <- as.data.frame(o_nca$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "ctrough")
cmin1_sim <- quantile(nca$PPORRES, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
cmin1_cmp <- data.frame(
  quantile = c("25th", "median", "75th"),
  simulated = as.numeric(cmin1_sim),
  table4 = c(62.8, 86.9, 105.6)
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / table4 - 1))
knitr::kable(cmin1_cmp, digits = 1)

stopifnot(
  # The simulated median trough falls inside the Table 4 interquartile range.
  cmin1_sim[["50%"]] > 62.8, cmin1_sim[["50%"]] < 105.6
)
```

The simulated quartiles depend on the assumed body weight and tumour size and
on any difference between the pooled four-study PK population and the sarcoma
patients, so only the median is checked, against the Table 4 interquartile
range.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Time unit.** The tables do not state the unit of the baseline hazard. Days
  are taken from the "Time (Days)" axes of Figures 1a and 2a, and are confirmed
  by the doxorubicin-alone PFS median: $\ln 2 / 0.00604 = 115$ days, 3.8
  months, against the observed 4.1 months.
* **Covariate form.** The equations are not printed. The Results describe the
  ECOG effect as an 86.2% increase and the no-prior-line effect as a 58.3%
  decrease of the baseline hazard, matching the Table 2 estimates 0.862 and
  -0.583, so each enters as a factor $(1 + \theta \cdot indicator)$. The two
  factors are multiplied: the Results state each effect as an unconditional
  percentage change, which holds for every patient only in the multiplicative
  form.
* **Covariate coding.** "EGRP" is coded as `ECOG_GE1` (ECOG >= 1 versus 0) per
  the Results text, although randomisation was stratified as ECOG 0-1 versus 2.
  "PRVTRT" is coded as `LINE_1L`, equal to 1 for patients with no prior line of
  treatment, per the Results text.
* **Drug effect.** "Inhibitory EMAX" with a Hill coefficient, applied "as a
  fractional decrease to the hazard function", is encoded as
  $1 - I_{max} C^{\gamma} / (EC_{50}^{\gamma} + C^{\gamma})$; Figures 1b and 2b
  confirm a hazard ratio of 1 at zero exposure and a plateau at $1 - I_{max}$.
  The paper's EMAX is named `limax` here because it is an inhibitory fraction.
* **Typeset standard errors.** Table 3 prints the %SEE of three PFS estimates
  as "2-52", "15-4" and "6-15", read as 2.52, 15.4 and 6.15. Standard errors
  do not enter the model.
* **Exposure distribution.** The virtual cohort draws exposures uniformly within
  each Table 4 quartile range. The real distribution (histograms of Figures 1b
  and 2b) is not uniform within quartiles.
* **No random effects or residual error.** The paper reports none; the models
  return the survival probability `sur`, the hazard and its closed-form median.
* **Safety.** The exposure-safety analysis (Table 4) is a tabulation of adverse
  event rates by exposure quartile with no fitted model, so nothing from it is
  packaged.
* **Errata.** No erratum was found for this article (Europe PMC, checked
  2026-11-25).
